meta.note: Whole constructions, not words. Speech is assembled from chunks; a learner who knows every word in 'dá para pagar aqui?' still cannot produce it. These are the chunks you reuse daily in Madeira.

cards.trans: is it possible to...? / can we...?
cards.note: the everyday way to ask if something is doable; textbooks never teach it
cards.ex_trans: Can I pay by card?

cards.note: pt-PT prefers ter de over ter que
cards.ex_trans: Sorry, I have to get going.

cards.note: the universal agreement noise; often just 'tá bem'
cards.ex_trans: Tomorrow at nine? All right.

cards.note: what you say when someone apologises
cards.ex_trans: You came late? Never mind.

cards.note: far more common in Portugal than talvez
cards.ex_trans: Maybe I'll go tomorrow.

cards.note: agreement with a shrug; you will hear it constantly
cards.ex_trans: Everything is expensive. — Yeah, tell me about it.

cards.note: the national approach to planning
cards.ex_t: Ainda não sei. Logo se vê.
cards.ex_trans: I don't know yet. We'll see.

cards.note: polite yes in shops and offices
cards.ex_trans: Can you help me? — Of course.

cards.note: said when giving way or handing something over
cards.ex_trans: Please, come in.

cards.trans: by the way, while we're at it
cards.note: adds a request to one already in progress
cards.ex_t: Já agora, traz-me também um café.
cards.ex_trans: While you're at it, bring me a coffee too.

cards.note: valer a pena = to be worth it
cards.ex_trans: It's not worth waiting.

cards.note: in a shop, better than the bare procuro
cards.ex_t: Estou à procura de um apartamento T2.
cards.ex_trans: I'm looking for a two-bedroom flat.

cards.note: demorar = to take time
cards.ex_trans: How long does it take on foot?

cards.note: clitic attaches to the infinitive — a pt-PT hallmark
cards.ex_trans: Excuse me, can you help me?

cards.note: your most useful sentence for the first year
cards.ex_t: Como se diz isto em português?
cards.ex_trans: How do you say this in Portuguese?

cards.note: querer dizer = to mean
cards.ex_trans: Sorry, what does 'avariado' mean?

cards.note: estar a + infinitive; Brazilians would say estou só olhando
cards.ex_t: Precisa de ajuda? — Obrigado, estou só a ver.
cards.ex_trans: Do you need help? — Thanks, I'm just looking.

cards.note: how you close a purchase
cards.ex_trans: I'll take this one, please.

cards.note: asked constantly in markets and taxis
cards.ex_trans: Do you have change for twenty euros?

cards.trans: I'd like to book an appointment
cards.note: the imperfect queria is the polite form
cards.ex_t: Boa tarde, queria marcar uma consulta.
cards.ex_trans: Good afternoon, I'd like to book an appointment.

cards.note: doer works backwards: the pain does the hurting to you
cards.ex_trans: It hurts here, on the right side.

cards.note: false friend — nothing to do with constipation, which is prisão de ventre
cards.ex_trans: I'm not going to work, I have a cold.

cards.note: answered with há: moro cá há dois anos
cards.ex_t: Há quanto tempo mora na Madeira?
cards.ex_trans: How long have you lived in Madeira?

cards.trans: I've lived here for two years
cards.note: há for elapsed time, present tense — not the past
cards.ex_t: Moro cá há dois anos e ainda estou a aprender.
cards.ex_trans: I've lived here two years and I'm still learning.

cards.trans: the lift is out of order
cards.note: avariado is the word on every broken machine in Portugal
cards.ex_t: Outra vez? O elevador está avariado.
cards.ex_trans: Again? The lift is out of order.

cards.note: há = there is / there are, one form for both
cards.ex_t: Desde ontem que não há água quente.
cards.ex_trans: There's been no hot water since yesterday.

cards.note: podia is softer than pode — worth the extra syllable
cards.ex_trans: Sorry, could you speak more slowly?

cards.note: say this early and people slow down for you
cards.ex_t: Ainda estou a aprender português, desculpe.
cards.ex_trans: I'm still learning Portuguese, sorry.

cards.note: the first question in every Portuguese public office
cards.ex_trans: Good morning. Do you have an appointment?

cards.trans: I need to sort this out
cards.note: tratar de = to deal with, the bureaucracy verb
cards.ex_t: Preciso de tratar disto antes de sexta.
cards.ex_trans: I need to sort this out before Friday.

cards.note: ficar bem = to suit; also fica-te bem informally
cards.ex_trans: Does this jacket suit me?

cards.note: the polite exit from any sales pitch
cards.ex_trans: Thanks, I'll think about it.

cards.note: estar à espera de = to be waiting for
cards.ex_t: Desculpe, está à espera de alguém?
cards.ex_trans: Excuse me, are you waiting for someone?

cards.note: the politest way to ask a favour
cards.ex_trans: Would you mind closing the window?

cards.ex_t: Vou lá de vez em quando.
cards.ex_trans: I go there from time to time.

cards.note: on every official notice about dates
cards.ex_t: A partir de segunda-feira o horário muda.
cards.ex_trans: Starting Monday the schedule changes.

cards.note: estar a + infinitive again; Brazilians say está chovendo
cards.ex_t: Leva o guarda-chuva, está a chover.
cards.ex_trans: Take the umbrella, it's raining.

cards.note: the é que construction is everywhere in spoken pt-PT
cards.ex_t: O que é que aconteceu ontem?
cards.ex_trans: What happened yesterday?

cards.note: softer than não sei
cards.ex_t: Não sei bem, tenho de confirmar.
cards.ex_trans: I'm not quite sure, I need to check.

cards.trans: it's over there at the end
cards.note: the answer you'll get when asking where something is
cards.ex_t: A casa de banho fica ali ao fundo.
cards.ex_trans: The toilet is over there at the end.
